equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.context: The S&P/TSX Composite closed at 33,833 on May 15, down 0.72% on the week. The index gave ground as the loonie eased to 0.7264 against the U.S. dollar and following the April CPI print of +2.8% year-over-year released May 19, the highest reading in roughly two years, which firmed expectations the Bank of Canada will hold its 2.25% overnight rate at its next decision2. The materials and energy sub-indices diverged from the broader tape: copper at US$6.32/lb (+36.21% year-over-year) and gold at US$4,497.00/oz (+41.33% year-over-year) underpinned resource names, while WTI at US$103.02/bbl (+64.33% year-over-year) supported the energy weighting amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption11. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the resource complex to 390 mining projects valued at $227.11B and 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.58B. If copper and gold sustain current levels, the 390 tracked mining projects would retain the revenue assumptions cited in public filings, while the 35 NAICS-21 mining and extraction projects carrying $81.39B in tracked value would maintain the cash-flow profile underpinning their development timelines18. Mining and quarrying GDP rose +3.6% year-over-year against a manufacturing contraction of -3.1%, a divergence the index reflected through its sector weighting; the database tracks 38 manufacturing projects totalling $62.19B exposed to that contraction8.

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.context: The S&P 500 stood at 7,339, up 6.65% measured against a sparse March baseline series. The move came after the Federal Reserve held the federal funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29 in an 8-4 split, the most dissents since October 1992, with markets pricing the range holding through year-end following the decision16. March U.S. CPI registered +3.3% year-over-year with core at +2.6%, and the FOMC statement attributed part of elevated inflation to higher global energy prices, framing the index reading against the energy-led inflation regime carried through the equity tape16. The level marks the highest print on the available series since the March reference point.

equities.name: Dow Jones
equities.context: The Dow Jones Industrial Average was at 49,438, up 6.19% against the March baseline series. The industrials-weighted benchmark moved as the Fed held rates steady on April 29 and the Kevin Warsh appointment took effect May 15, with the central bank citing higher global energy prices in its inflation assessment16. The print sits at the highest level on the available series since the March reference, recorded as WTI rose to US$103.02/bbl, up 64.33% year-over-year amid the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption11.

equities.name: NASDAQ
equities.context: The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,090, down 0.70% on the week. The technology-weighted index diverged from the broader U.S. tape as the Fed held the funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29 and markets priced no change through year-end, leaving rate-sensitive growth names without a downward shift in discount-rate expectations following the decision16. The weekly decline contrasts with the highest-level prints recorded on the S&P 500 and Dow series over the same window since the March reference point.
